review.summary: A referral programme looks worth running alongside your existing channels, but only as a modest addition. With your 3,000 paying customers, it would add 17 new customers in a year, 0.6% growth on today's base, and £61,719 of yearly revenue, for a programme cost of £10,972 that pays back in 2.1 months.
review.lever: The number that matters most is the share of referred people who sign up, currently 15%. Raising it to 20% would bring in 5.7 extra customers in a year and £20,644 of extra yearly revenue.
risks: The gain is small in absolute terms, so the programme will not change your growth on its own, and the result depends on the Typical assumptions holding for your business.
Your 12% of customers lost a year is a steady drain that referrals will not fix, so retention work may matter at least as much as the programme.
actions: Start with a small test for a few months before committing the full £400 a month running cost.
Work on the sign-up experience for referred people first, since turning more of them into sign-ups has the biggest effect.
Track how many customers actually refer each month against the 5% assumption, then recheck the 2.1 months payback with real figures.
